source.author: verg
source.text: Ecce autem elapsus Pyrrhi de caede Polites, unus natorum Priami, per tela, per hostis porticibus longis fugit, et vacua atria lustrat saucius: illum ardens infesto volnere Pyrrhus insequitur, iam iamque manu tenet et premit hasta.
source.text_original: Ecce autem elapsus Pyrrhi de caede Polites, / unus natorum Priami, per tela, per hostis / porticibus longis fugit, et vacua atria lustrat / saucius: illum ardens infesto volnere Pyrrhus / insequitur, iam iamque manu tenet et premit hasta.
source.text_english: But look, Polites, one of Priam’s sons, having slipped away from Pyrrhus’ slaughter, flees through the weapons, through the enemy, along the long colonnades, and wounded ranges through the empty courts; fiery Pyrrhus pursues him with hostile wound, and now, now already holds him with his hand and presses him with his spear.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Bistonas ad meritos cum cornua saeva Thyoneus torsit et infelix iam mille furoribus Haemus, iam Rhodopes nemora alta gemunt, talem incita longis porticibus coniunxque fugit natique Lycurgum.
reuse.text_original: Bistonas ad meritos cum cornua saeva Thyoneus / torsit et infelix iam mille furoribus Haemus, / iam Rhodopes nemora alta gemunt, talem incita longis / porticibus coniunxque fugit natique Lycurgum.
reuse.text_english: When Thyoneus had turned his savage horns against the Bistones as they deserved, and cursed Haemus now groaned beneath a thousand frenzies, and now the lofty woods of Rhodope groaned, his wife and sons fled from such a Lycurgus, driven on through the long colonnades.
